name: Residual resistivity ratio of high-purity niobium (273 K / 4.2 K) with field suppression of superconductivity and Kohler extrapolation
plain_name: Grade niobium purity by comparing its electrical resistance at ice and liquid-helium temperatures
description: NIST compared RRR methods on 14 Nb samples, using voltage-tap resistance at 273 K and 4.2 K with fields up to 5-8 T.
keywords: Grade niobium purity by comparing its electrical resistance at ice and liquid-helium temperatures

sources.citation: Splett, Vecchia, Goodrich, J. Res. NIST 116(1) 489-504 (2011)

requirements.rationale: RRR uses resistance at 273 K and at 4.2 K.
Field data up to 5 T were used to suppress superconductivity and extrapolate.
Resistance is measured between voltage taps.
The low point is the liquid-helium boiling point; a dry 4.2 K system would also work.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
